nodes.description: In the LRP4-related form (sclerosteosis 2), sclerostin is produced but cannot act. Bone-overgrowth-associated LRP4 variants impair the receptor's interaction with sclerostin and its sclerostin-facilitator function, so Wnt/beta-catenin signaling in osteoblasts escapes sclerostin restraint by a different route than in SOST loss. Because sclerostin is still made but not retained or presented in bone, circulating sclerostin is raised rather than absent, which is the biochemical feature that distinguishes this form from SOST-related sclerosteosis.

nodes.description: SOST encodes sclerostin, a secreted glycoprotein with a cysteine-knot motif that functions as an antagonist of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway by binding to LRP5/LRP6 coreceptors on osteoblasts. Loss-of-function mutations abolish sclerostin production, removing the physiological brake on bone formation.

genetic_context.description: Biallelic SOST loss-of-function variants (two nonsense and one splice-site variant in the original sclerosteosis cohorts) abolish sclerostin production. Van Buchem disease is caused instead by a biallelic 52-kb regulatory deletion downstream of SOST, which is why it is modeled as a separate subtype of this entry rather than as another SOST coding allele.
